verdict: Where the terminal cites, it cites well: 35 of 42 sampled figures are on the cited page as written, the law and the cases rest on primary sources (CPS, DOJ, legislation.gov.uk, the IRS, the Geneva free port’s own accounts to the thousand francs), and the Currents and the Walls are the real asset. But that strength sits in the research bundle, not in the engines that ‘solve’. The Brief composes a confident memo from wrong defaults — the United States for any city it does not know, Sotheby’s for every house, a 0% seller’s commission, UK and US playbooks for Berlin, Dubai, Mumbai and Mexico City — it continues past its own closed wall into a shipping quote and a letter for a prohibited sale, it cannot see ivory, it screens no name, and it prints ‘the median’ from one lot; the central table of 154 lots carries no source at all; the fee engine disagrees with the research it is built on; and the instrument that tells the reader how much is verified does not count the half of the page where most of the unverified lines are. The 25 briefs scored 2.28 of 5 — the engine is right where the research is deep (New York, London, Paris, Milan, the sanctions files) and silently wrong everywhere else. This is a well-sourced library with a memo generator in front of it, not yet a foundation for ‘deep, precise analysis of any request in the field’.
